mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% in the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity and supply, which boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same period, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over three months signals deflationary pressures, which increases the real value of debt and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL decreased by more than 0.5% in the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 2% QoQ and RSAFS increases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which encourages investment in riskier assets like equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods where FEDFUNDS was below 1%.
